chunks: Al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) said: My father narrated to me from my grandfather (peace be upon both of them) that the Commander of the Faithful (blessings of God upon him) said:
Who can guarantee you one day a brother who is completely [without flaw]? And which of men is without blemish?

key_terms.أخيك كله: Your brother in his entirety — implying a friend who is perfect in all aspects
key_terms.المهذب: One who is refined, cultivated, or free from moral defects; a person without flaws

ai.seo_question: What did Imam Ali say about the imperfection of men and friendship?
ai.summary: Imam Sadiq (AS) transmits through his father Imam Baqir (AS) and grandfather Imam Zayn al-Abidin (AS) a saying attributed to Imam Ali (AS) about human imperfection. The saying counsels realistic expectations in friendship — no man is entirely free of flaws. This wisdom, shared in a gathering in Mashhad of Imam al-Rida, reflects the Imams' practical ethical guidance: true brotherhood means accepting human fallibility rather than demanding perfection.

en.bilal-muhammad: Al-Sadiq (as) said: My father narrated to me from my grandfather (as). Amir al-Mu’minin (s) said:
Which of your brothers is perfect? Which man is free of flaws?
